title: Add JSON schema + CI validation for status component registry
author: Allison Grant
description: This PR introduces a JSON Schema for the public status-page component registry and adds validation in CI so registry changes fail fast when they are malformed or violate taxonomy rules. Motivation: we’re using the registry as a source-of-truth for component ids/display names/ownership and rollout flags as part of the Status page transparency upgrades effort; recent incidents and hotfixes showed that small typos (ids, missing fields, inconsistent region/capability labels) can cause misclassification and customer-facing status inaccuracies. What’s included: (1) New schema file `statuspage/component-registry.schema.json` that defines required fields and constraints for each component entry: `component_id` (kebab-case, stable, unique), `display_name` (human readable), `product_area` (hosted_api|streaming|embeddings|reranking|console|dedicated_control_plane), `regions` (allowed set), `capabilities` (allowed set), `ownership` (team + slack channel), and `rollout` flags (`public_enabled`, `console_link_enabled`, `auto_updates_enabled`) with defaults. (2) Validation script `scripts/validate-status-component-registry.ts` (AJV) that validates `statuspage/component-registry.json` against the schema and additionally enforces a few cross-field rules that JSON Schema can’t express cleanly (e.g., no duplicate display_name within the same product_area+region group, `public_enabled=false` components must not have `console_link_enabled=true`, and region list must be non-empty for region-scoped product areas). (3) CI wiring: adds a `statuspage-registry-validate` job to the existing checks and runs it on PRs that touch `statuspage/**`. (4) Developer ergonomics: `npm run validate:statuspage-registry` command, plus README updates describing how to add a new component safely and how to handle deprecated/renamed ids (no renames; add new id and mark old id `public_enabled=false` only after deprecation window). Notes: This does not change runtime/statuspage behavior directly; it only adds guardrails for future registry edits. Follow-ups will update incident-bot + gateway metrics tagging to rely on the validated ids (tracked in ENG-4822/ENG-4830).

review_conversation: Rafael Mendes (review): Can we be stricter about `component_id` format? We’ve had camelCase creep in. Also please ensure we document the rename/deprecation policy since customers bookmark component names. Allison Grant (author): Added regex for kebab-case and clarified policy in README: ids are immutable; deprecate via `public_enabled=false` after 30d and keep mapping until downstream tooling is updated. Aisha Bello (review): Cross-field rule: if `public_enabled=false`, should we also require `auto_updates_enabled=false`? Otherwise the automation might try to post. Allison Grant (author): Good call; added rule and test coverage. Christine Wong (review): The allowed `regions` list should match the taxonomy doc; we currently include `ap-south-1` in some working notes but I don’t think it’s live. Suggest locking to the currently public regions only. Allison Grant (author): Updated allowed regions to `us-east`, `us-west`, `eu-west` per current public status page and added a comment on how to expand (schema update + comms review). Naomi Feldman (security/compliance): Ownership fields include Slack channels; ok to keep internal-only but make sure this repo isn’t mirrored publicly. Allison Grant (author): Confirmed internal-only; also added note in README that ownership is internal metadata. Final review: LGTM from Rafael/Aisha/Christine; Naomi approved with note.
release_notes: Internal-only: adds schema + CI validation for status component registry to reduce status-page mapping errors.
